description: Test cases covering scope inference, error reclassification, evidence sufficiency, multi-tier correlation, output formatting, freshness gating, volume-drop detection, workload inference, and sensor deployment caveats. Assertions target the current output spec in reference/output-templates.md: Default mode for interactive checks (H2 title, bold verdict line with middle-dot separator, verdict-first findings bullets, backticked identifiers, console deep-links, no HSI/confidence/YAML in the body), Detailed mode only when explicitly triggered (tagging, scheduled, audit, 'full report'), and Quick-look mode for 'tldr'-style asks. Each prompt represents a realistic question a customer might ask their AI agent in an environment with ExtraHop MCP connected.

evals.name: environment-implicit-scope
evals.prompt: Run a health check on the network.
evals.expected_output: An environment-scope assessment in Default mode. H2 title `## Health Check: Environment`, a bold verdict line using the middle-dot separator (e.g. `**Normal** · Last 24 hours · 3 sensors`), a one-sentence problem statement, 4–6 verdict-first findings bullets, a `**Key insight.**` paragraph, and (when not Normal) `What to do` / `Drill in further` sections. Any error reclassification (e.g. NXDOMAIN excluded from DNS) is reflected in the bullet or Key insight. No HSI percentage, no confidence line, no YAML footer, no 'What changed' table in the body — those belong to Detailed mode only.

assertions.text: Title is an H2 `## Health Check: Environment` (not H1, not the Detailed-mode `**Overall status:` opener)
A bold verdict line directly under the title uses the middle-dot separator `·` and the time window (e.g. `**Normal** · Last 24 hours`)
Findings are verdict-first bullets: bold verdict word, italicized category, em-dash, one sentence each
Uses status values from the allowed vocabulary only: Normal, Warning, Degraded, Insufficient Evidence (title case in visible output)
Calls out any error reclassification (e.g. NXDOMAIN excluded from the DNS actionable rate) in a bullet or the Key insight
Default mode body does NOT include an HSI percentage, a Confidence line, a 'What changed' table, or a YAML footer
Device and device-group identifiers appear in backticks. Device identifiers remain unlinked. Device-group links use the available console FQDN; never fabricates URLs.
No box-drawing characters (═, ┌, ┐, ─, │, ┴, ┬, └, ┘) in the output

evals.name: device-symptom-language
evals.prompt: Users are saying web-app-01 is slow. Can you check what's going on?
evals.expected_output: Device-scope assessment of web-app-01 in Default mode. If latency or 5xx is elevated, the skill follows Playbook 1 and checks backend DB latency before finalizing. If a downstream cause is identified, the Key insight attributes root cause to the downstream tier and the downstream device is promoted as a first-class 'Drill in further' item. Role-aware: web-app-01's primary categories are HTTP, SSL, TCP latency; TCP retransmissions are secondary.

assertions.text: Recognizes the symptom-language as a device check on web-app-01 (does NOT default to environment scope)
If HTTP issues are found, attempts a downstream check (backend DB latency or TCP to backends) before finalizing the verdict
If a downstream device is identified as root cause, promotes it as a first-class 'Drill in further' item (e.g. 'Run a full health check on db-prod-02')
Role weighting is applied — TCP retransmissions are treated as secondary, not primary, for an http_server role
Output follows Default-mode format from reference/output-templates.md (H2 title, bold verdict line with `·`, verdict-first bullets, Key insight, What to do / Drill in further)

evals.name: protocol-fleet-dns
evals.prompt: How is DNS performing across our environment?
evals.expected_output: Protocol-scope DNS fleet check in Default mode. Discovers DNS servers by role. Capture-level screening first, then samples up to 10 devices. Uses two-pass classification: queries `dns_server:rsp_rcode` and excludes NXDOMAIN. Distinguishes authoritative vs recursive DNS in the latency assessment if mixed roles are present. Ranks per-device results worst-first. When the fleet is bimodal, leads with the shape (e.g. 'most healthy, 3 degraded') rather than an average.

assertions.text: Performs two-pass DNS classification (queries the rcode breakdown)
Reclassifies NXDOMAIN as benign and reports the actionable rate (SERVFAIL + FORMERR)
Reports raw and reclassified error rates if both are non-trivial
If servers serve different roles (authoritative vs recursive), applies the correct latency threshold per server
Ranks per-device results worst-first (lowest health first) when listing them
If the fleet is bimodal, the problem statement leads with the shape ('most of the fleet is healthy, but N are degraded'), not a single average

evals.name: low-activity-insufficient-evidence
evals.prompt: Check Kerberos health on our domain controllers over the last hour.
evals.expected_output: If Kerberos response volume is below 100 across the fleet (e.g., off-hours, low activity), the skill returns Insufficient Evidence rather than Normal or Warning. The output explains what's missing with specific numbers (e.g., 'only 31 responses observed, minimum gate is 100') and offers a 'Drill in further' to rerun with a longer window or during business hours.

assertions.text: If the minimum activity gate (100 responses) is not met on the driving category, the verdict is Insufficient Evidence, not Normal or Warning
Output explains why evidence is insufficient with specific numbers
No HSI percentage is shown in the Default-mode body
Includes a 'Drill in further' item suggesting a longer window or different time

evals.name: tagging-mode-natural-language
evals.prompt: Run a health check on dc-01, web-lb-01, and dns-primary and tag the unhealthy ones.
evals.expected_output: Device-scope check on the three named devices. Tagging mode is enabled by the natural-language trigger ('tag the unhealthy ones'), which selects Detailed mode output. For each device, after assessment: clears stale Health-Warning and Health-Degraded tags, then applies the appropriate tag if the device is Warning or Degraded. In an interactive session, confirms before applying tag changes. The report includes a TAGGING SUMMARY listing devices tagged, cleared, and any errors.

assertions.text: Recognizes 'tag the unhealthy ones' as a tagging-mode trigger and uses Detailed-mode output
Tags only devices that are Warning or Degraded; clears tags on Normal devices
Output includes a TAGGING SUMMARY section listing what was tagged and cleared
In an interactive session, confirms with the user before applying tag changes

evals.name: multi-tier-root-cause
evals.prompt: Investigate web-app-01 — HTTP errors are up.
evals.expected_output: Device check on web-app-01 in Default mode. After confirming HTTP 5xx is elevated, follows Playbook 1: checks `db_server:tprocess` on backend DBs and `tcp:rto_out` on web→db links. If the downstream DB is also degraded, the web-tier verdict still reflects observable HTTP errors, but the Key insight explains the chain and attributes root cause to the DB, the 'What to do' actions target the DB tier, and the downstream device gets a first-class 'Drill in further' item. The same root cause is not double-counted as two unrelated findings.

assertions.text: After identifying elevated HTTP 5xx, queries downstream DB latency or TCP to backends
If a downstream cause is identified, the Key insight explicitly names the downstream tier/device as root cause
'What to do' actions target the actual root cause (DB on-call), not just the symptom tier
The downstream device (e.g. db-prod-02) gets a first-class 'Drill in further' item (e.g. 'Run a full health check on db-prod-02')
Does not double-count the same root cause as two separate unrelated findings

evals.name: asymmetric-routing-caveat
evals.prompt: Check overall network health for the past hour.
evals.expected_output: Environment check in Default mode. If a sensor's `tcp:unidirectional_flows` exceeds 25% of total flows, the skill does NOT issue TCP-based Warning/Degraded verdicts for that sensor. Instead it folds an asymmetric-routing caveat into the Key insight and recommends investigating sensor deployment as a 'What to do' action.

assertions.text: Queries `tcp:unidirectional_flows` at capture level
If unidirectional_flows exceeds 25% on a sensor, TCP-based verdicts for that sensor are downgraded or suppressed
When asymmetric routing is detected, the output includes a 'What to do' recommendation to investigate sensor deployment
The asymmetric-routing limitation is surfaced in the Key insight (Default mode folds Medium/Low confidence into Key insight rather than a separate Confidence line)

evals.name: ambiguous-scope-defaults-to-environment
evals.expected_output: Ambiguous prompt with no specific target. The skill defaults to environment scope and runs the standard environment procedure in Default mode, then offers 'Drill in further' items for narrower investigation into a device or protocol.

assertions.text: Defaults to environment scope (does not ask for clarification before producing anything)
Produces a complete environment report in Default-mode format (H2 title, bold verdict line, verdict-first bullets, Key insight)
Offers 'Drill in further' items for narrower investigation

evals.name: kerberos-preauth-required-false-positive
evals.expected_output: Device check on a domain controller in Default mode. If raw Kerberos `rsp_error` is around 8% (typical AD environment), the breakdown shows that the vast majority (90%+) is `KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED`, which is benign. The skill reports Kerberos as Normal and explicitly notes the reclassification (raw rate vs actionable rate) in the bullet or Key insight.

assertions.text: Queries the Kerberos error breakdown (`kerberos_server_detail:error_msg`), not just `rsp_error`
Reclassifies `KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED` as benign and excludes it from the actionable rate
Reports Kerberos status as Normal (not Warning) when the actionable rate is < 1%
Output explicitly notes the reclassification (raw rate vs actionable rate)

evals.name: silent-outage-volume-drop
evals.prompt: Quick check on our DNS servers.
evals.expected_output: Protocol fleet check on DNS. If a DNS server's request volume has dropped > 5× from baseline (silent-outage signature) while error rates on residual traffic look fine, the skill issues Warning or Degraded for that server on a request-volume finding. The problem statement / Key insight calls out a possible service outage, maintenance, or isolation, recommends verifying reachability as a 'What to do' action, and checks whether peer DNS servers absorbed the displaced load.

assertions.text: Queries request volume (`dns:rsp` or `dns_server:rsp` count) alongside error metrics
Detects the > 5× volume drop on the affected server as a finding even when the error rate is normal
Verdict is Warning or Degraded (not Normal) for the volume-drop case
Problem statement or Key insight mentions the silent-outage / service-down / maintenance possibility
Recommends verifying reachability of the affected server as a 'What to do' action
Checks whether peer DNS servers are absorbing the displaced load and notes it

evals.name: stale-data-freshness-gate
evals.prompt: Run a health check on the network.
evals.expected_output: The pre-assessment freshness check finds that the most recent capture-level data is > 10 minutes old. The skill does NOT report Normal regardless of what the stale metrics show — instead the report IS the freshness warning: verdict Insufficient Evidence with `· Data stale`, an explanation of the staleness with a specific duration, and 'What to do' actions to investigate sensor/appliance connectivity. Staleness is not buried in a confidence caveat.

assertions.text: Queries data freshness (e.g., most recent net:bytes bucket timestamp) before running the assessment
If data is > 10 minutes stale, returns Insufficient Evidence regardless of metric values
Does NOT issue a Normal verdict on stale data
The report leads with the freshness problem (e.g. verdict line `**Insufficient Evidence** · Data stale`) and states a specific staleness duration
Recommends a 'What to do' action to investigate ExtraHop sensor/appliance connectivity

evals.name: data-warehouse-oltp-threshold-misapplication
evals.prompt: Check the health of dwh-prod-01 (it's our Snowflake proxy).
evals.expected_output: Device check on a database server with naming and workload patterns indicating OLAP / data warehouse. The skill infers the workload type (high rsp_ttlb, multi-second baseline tprocess) and applies the OLAP latency thresholds (< 5s normal, > 30s degraded) rather than OLTP thresholds. A 2-second p50 latency does NOT produce a Degraded verdict on an OLAP server, and the workload inference is noted in the Key insight.

assertions.text: Infers workload type before applying latency thresholds (queries rsp_ttlb or notes naming/role signals)
Applies OLAP latency thresholds when the workload is OLAP (does NOT use the 100ms / 500ms OLTP bands)
Notes the workload inference in the Key insight (e.g. 'workload type: OLAP / data warehouse')
Does NOT issue Warning or Degraded on multi-second latency that is normal for OLAP

evals.name: low-volume-baseline-percentage-noise
evals.prompt: Check ldap-secondary-01 for the last hour.
evals.expected_output: Device check on a low-volume LDAP server. If baseline volume was below 100 responses, the skill does NOT report a percentage change like 'errors up 233% (3 → 10)' — that's noise. Instead it falls back to peer comparison (other LDAP servers in the fleet) or reports raw counts, and notes the methodology choice in the Key insight.

assertions.text: Checks baseline volume before computing a percentage change
If baseline volume is below 100 responses, does NOT report a percentage change like '+233% (3→10)'
Falls back to peer comparison or raw counts when the baseline is too small
Notes the methodology choice in the Key insight ('baseline volume insufficient' or 'compared to peer LDAP servers')

evals.name: quick-look-tldr
evals.expected_output: User explicitly requests a brief format ('tldr'), which triggers Quick-look mode: H2 title, the bold verdict line with the time window, one problem-statement sentence, and an offer to elaborate. No findings list, no Key insight, no next-steps sections, no HSI, and no multi-column tables.

assertions.text: Recognizes 'tldr' as a Quick-look mode trigger
Output is just the H2 title, the bold verdict line, one problem-statement sentence, and an offer to elaborate
Output does NOT include a findings list, a Key insight paragraph, next-steps sections, or any multi-column table
Does NOT include an HSI line (Quick-look never shows HSI)
Offers a follow-up to ask for the full report or to drill into a specific finding

evals.name: detailed-mode-full-report-with-hsi
evals.prompt: Run a detailed health check on web-app-01 for the last hour and include the full structured report.
evals.expected_output: The explicit 'detailed' / 'full structured report' request triggers Detailed mode on a device check of web-app-01 with sufficient activity (> 100 HTTP responses). Detailed mode includes the Overall status / User impact / Likely cause opener, a Confidence line with a decision aid, an HSI line with percentage and band, a 'What changed' table, per-category subsections, and a collapsed machine-readable YAML footer. The HSI decomposes into Satisfied / Tolerating / Frustrated buckets using the HTTP application thresholds (T=200ms, 4T=800ms) with 5xx treated as Frustrated.

assertions.text: Recognizes 'detailed' / 'full structured report' as a Detailed-mode trigger
Output includes the Detailed-mode opener (Overall status / User impact / Likely cause) and a Confidence line with a decision aid
Output includes an HSI line with a percentage and band label, decomposed into Satisfied / Tolerating / Frustrated bucket counts in the body or YAML footer
Bucket classification uses HTTP application thresholds (T=200ms) and treats 5xx errors as Frustrated; HSI ≈ (Satisfied + 0.5×Tolerating)/Total within rounding tolerance
Output includes a 'What changed' table and a collapsed machine-readable YAML footer (in a <details> block or similar)

evals.name: account-lockout-first-class-finding
evals.prompt: Check dc-east-01 for the last hour.
evals.expected_output: Device check on a domain controller in Default mode. If `account_lockout` is non-trivial (≥ 5 lockouts OR ≥ 3× baseline rate), the lockout appears as its own findings bullet — not buried inside a general Kerberos sentence. The lockout pattern (broad vs concentrated, with/without PREAUTH_FAILED) informs the recommended 'What to do' action (security paging, MFA check, or service-account rotation).

assertions.text: If the account_lockout count is non-trivial, it appears as its own findings bullet
The output characterizes the lockout pattern (broad vs concentrated, coincident with other auth signals)
Recommended 'What to do' actions match the pattern: security paging for a broad spike, service-account rotation for a steady low rate, MFA upstream check for a concentrated spike

evals.name: virtualized-sensor-vpc-mirror-loss
evals.prompt: Why are we seeing so many TCP retransmissions on our cloud sensor?
evals.expected_output: Investigation of TCP retransmissions on a cloud-deployed sensor. If unidirectional_flows is broadly distributed (not concentrated on one peer) and setup_time isn't uniformly elevated, the skill recognizes this as a likely VPC traffic-mirroring loss signature rather than a real network problem, and recommends investigating mirror capacity / sensor deployment quality as a 'What to do' action rather than issuing a Degraded network verdict.

assertions.text: Considers sensor deployment quality (VPC mirroring, SPAN oversubscription) when TCP issues are observed on a cloud sensor
If unidirectional_flows is high AND broadly distributed, characterizes the finding as a likely sensor-deployment issue rather than a network problem
Recommends investigating mirror capacity / SPAN configuration as a 'What to do' action
Does NOT issue a Degraded network verdict when the evidence is consistent with sensor-side packet loss

evals.name: device-links-deferred-with-current-mcp
evals.prompt: Run a health check on web-app-01 and link it to the console.
evals.expected_output: Completes the health check on web-app-01 with a plain backticked identifier. Briefly explains that reliable device links are not currently supported.

assertions.text: Completes the health check and keeps web-app-01 unlinked
Briefly explains the limitation because the user requested a device link
Does not attempt to construct a device URL or fetch metadata solely for one

evals.name: device-links-deferred-despite-pasted-url
evals.prompt: This link works for dc-01: https://tenant.cloud.extrahop.com/extrahop/#/metrics/devices/a1b2c3d4e5f6478899aabbccddeeff00.0123456789abcdef/kerberos-server?delta_type&from=1&interval_type=DAY&until=0. Now run a health check on web-app-02 and link it to the console.
evals.expected_output: Completes the health check on web-app-02 with a plain backticked identifier, despite the pasted device URL. Briefly explains that reliable device links are not currently supported.

assertions.text: Completes the health check and keeps all device identifiers unlinked
Does not reuse the pasted device URL or its IDs to construct device links
Briefly explains the device-link limitation
